source.title: Dead Weights, Live Signals: Feedforward Graphs of Frozen Language Models
source.authors: M. Armstrong; Navid Ayoobi; Arjun Mukherjee

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures cross-architecture representational mapping with Ridge regression, using a different setup from the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper's own Ridge and shuffled-pair results measure cross-architecture geometric compatibility. Its benchmark scores, graph ablations, and gradient-flow results concern the task performance or trainability of the proposed graph, not whether representations converge; they are not rows. Other alignment values and scale claims attributed to prior work are cited results and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study independently measures linear cross-architecture mapping quality for frozen Llama and Qwen representations. Its Ridge and permutation-control results bear on V4 and the incomplete-alignment component of V7; the graph's task performance primarily uses representational compatibility.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' alignment interpretation: the offline mapping captures nontrivial cross-architecture geometry, and task training can refine useful projection directions. Their main conclusion concerns the frozen-model graph's benchmark gains, tractable gradients, and selective routing. They do not demonstrate a scale trend or directly measure alignment improvement after task training.
record.recipe_differences: Measures one cross-family LLM pair with Ridge regression on 50 factual questions; it does not reproduce the original sources' broader representation-convergence measurements.
record.code_released: not stated; training and evaluation code is described as provided as supplementary material.
record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2027 conference paper, as stated in the text.
record.problems: The direct alignment measurement uses only 50 question-answer pairs and one cross-family model pair. The authors note its R² is lower than a cited prior result and attribute this partly to the small fitting set, smaller models, and cross-family pairing. The paper reports single runs for its benchmark results, though those results are not direct alignment measurements.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded benchmark results and graph ablations (Sections 4–5) because they measure task accuracy or graph behavior rather than representation alignment. Excluded cited alignment and scale results because they are from prior work.

untested.parts: No alignment sweep over model size or capability; scale comparisons are attributed to prior work.
No vision-language alignment or paired image-caption experiment.
No comparison across initializations of the same architecture.

No demonstrated little-loss downstream substitution, held-out mapping protocol, layer stitching evaluation, relative representations, or mapping without paired data; direct mapping covers one model pair.
No identification or comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
No controlled variation of alignment metrics, metric settings, fitting datasets, or input distributions. Shuffled correspondence is a negative control.
No alignment plateau, causal test of shared training data or objectives, or comparison against a common-reality explanation.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source of the supplied versions. Benchmark scores, injection ablations, routing, and gradient norms do not independently measure convergence. The authors' explanations for the lower R² are hypotheses rather than controlled findings; comparisons with prior studies cannot establish metric, data, or scale dependence here.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no comparison of alignment across architectures, objectives, or data as models scale.
No vision-language model or paired image-caption alignment test.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations of the same architecture.
Tests one Ridge mapping on one cross-family Llama-Qwen pair; does not test stitching layers, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are measured.
Does not vary similarity measures, settings, or input distributions; the shuffled-pair control is not a metric- or data-sensitivity sweep.
The measured mapping indicates incomplete alignment for one model pair, but the study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct → Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Fit a Ridge regression mapping Llama representations to Qwen representations and measure R².
rows.note: The paper describes this as real and non-trivial alignment, but lower than the cited prior result for similar-scale cross-architecture pairs.
rows.check: The reported R² of 0.299 is correct. Partial describes V4's little-loss mapping claim; for V7, incomplete measured alignment is observed. The text does not specify the fitting/evaluation split, so this value cannot establish held-out interchangeability or an intrinsic ceiling on alignment.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct → Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Fit Ridge regression after randomly permuting the rows of the Qwen activation matrix.
rows.note: The authors say the negative control result supports semantic correspondence in the unpermuted mapping rather than an effect of marginal statistics.
rows.check: The reported R² of -0.243 is correct. This is a deliberately mismatched-pair control supporting interpretation of r1, not evidence that genuine paired representations fail to map. It does not independently measure V7's incomplete semantic alignment.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct to Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; 50 factual questions, depth 0.75, Ridge λ=1
relationships.reason: r1 reports positive but limited mapping quality (R²=0.299), qualifying little-loss interchangeability; r2's shuffled control scores -0.243.
relationships.display_finding: Mapping achieved R²=0.299 on 50 factual questions at depth 0.75 with ridge λ=1, compared with −0.243 for the shuffled control.

relationships.condition: Incomplete offline linear alignment in the tested Llama-Qwen pair
relationships.reason: r1's R²=0.299 shows substantially incomplete measured alignment under this fitting protocol; it does not establish a plateau or its causes.
relationships.display_finding: The fitted linear alignment achieved R²=0.299, demonstrating substantial incompleteness under the tested protocol.
